messages:
Sam: ran a quick nsys trace inside the k8s job to investigate the perf regression — seeing a ton of tiny kernel launches after KV cache misses, latency spikes on tail tokens. attaching notes.
Priya: can you paste the nsys timeline snippet? curious if it's a bunch of memcpy/launch overhead or actual GEMM work fragmentation.
Sam: snippet below (trimmed):
```
CPU  |  CUDA API  |  CUDA Kernel
0.0ms | cudaMemcpyAsync | memcpy_h2d (2us)
0.2ms | launch          | fused_gemm_128x64 (30us)
0.6ms | launch          | gemm_32x32        (12us)
1.0ms | launch          | memcpy_d2h (1us)
... many small launches chained when KV miss rate high
```
Sam: overall token latency jumps when kv cache miss ratio > 6%. Before regression it was <2% and fused kernels dominated.
Miguel: that looks like kernel selection fallback — maybe quantized path can't use TensorCores when sequence-length irregular, so runtime emits multiple smaller kernels. Did the trace show different cuBLAS kernels across runs?
Sam: yes — before: cublasLt_fused_gemm; after: cublasGemmEx + small memcpy + kernel launch overhead. NVTX shows fallback at model layer where cached KV shapes differ.
Nora: curious about the container trace bits — we saw some failed nvprof/nsys captures earlier due to file perms in /tmp/.nvidia or plugin mismatch. Any errors in the pod logs?
Sam: got this from the pod: 
"nsys: cannot open 'target.nsys-rep' for writing: Permission denied" and an earlier error: 
"nvidia-container-toolkit: failed to setup: incompatible plugin version 1.10 (need >=1.12)"
Priya: ah, that's likely why some profiling runs were partial. On k8s our sidecars run as non-root and the toolkit writes /run/nvidia/... needs write perms. For reproducible traces, run with either the new toolkit or mount /run/nvidia as writable.
devops-bot: recommended quick test: `kubectl run -it --rm --image=nvidia/cuda:12.1-toolkit --privileged --restart=Never gpu-debug -- nvidia-smi` to validate runtime. Also check node plugin version: `nvidia-container-cli --version` on the node.
Miguel: actionable checklist: 1) verify nvidia-container-toolkit >=1.12 on nodes, 2) run nsys with capture-range=cudaProfilerApi to avoid missing regions, 3) for container capture add `--cap-add SYS_PTRACE` or use privileged debug pod if host attach required, 4) ensure /tmp or /run/nvidia mounts writable for the user in container.
Priya: for the runtime side fix, we should log KV cache shape variance and add a batching heuristic to avoid emitting tiny kernels: i.e., postpone kernel selection until sequence-length for a micro-batch is stable or pad to block size for fused kernels. Also consider a small recompile cache keyed by sequence-length distribution.
Sam: I'll open a small PR with instrumentation and a repro job that toggles kv hit rate. includes scripts to run nsys inside the pod and a helper that retries with privileged mount. Posting commands in case others want to reproduce:
```bash
# debug pod with toolkit mount and writable run dir
kubectl run -it --rm --image=redwood/debug-gpu:latest gpu-debug --overrides='{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"gpu-debug","image":"redwood/debug-gpu:latest","securityContext":{"privileged":true},"volumeMounts":[{"name":"run-nvidia","mountPath":"/run/nvidia"}]}],"volumes":[{"name":"run-nvidia","emptyDir":{}}]}}' --restart=Never -- nvidia-smi
# inside pod: capture
nsys profile --output=/run/nvidia/trace --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --trace=cuda,osrt ./serve_bench --workload kv-toggle
```
Nora: thanks — when you open the PR tag me. Also add a k8s job YAML that reproduces the low/high kv hit cases so QE can run it in CI.
Sam: will do. TL;DR: regression caused by kernel-selection fallback + higher KV miss rate; some traces were noisy due to toolkit/container perms. Next: repro job, PR for batching/pad heuristic, node-toolkit version audit. :thumbsup:
